description: IR2 is Akatsuki’s 2-μm camera, using nightside atmospheric windows to trace Venus’s lower clouds and carbon monoxide. Its 2.02-μm channel probes dayside cloud-top altitude, while the 1.65-μm channel was used for zodiacal-light observations during cruise.
facility_description: Akatsuki, also called the Venus Climate Orbiter or PLANET-C, is JAXA’s Venus mission for studying the planet’s atmosphere using cameras at several wavelengths and radio occultation.
notes: Descriptions are paraphrased from live ISAS/JAXA instrument pages and the cited papers. DARTS About explicitly directs data users to ISAS Data Policy. Section 6 permits commercial and non-commercial reuse, requires ISAS/JAXA origin credit, asks users to identify and describe modifications, and preserves third-party restrictions. The DARTS acknowledgement is conditional on significant use of its service; general DARTS archive papers are not mandatory instrument citations. Filter files are PLANET-C calibration documents mirrored by NASA PDS. No instrument-specific extra redistribution restriction was found in the inspected inventories, labels or owner pages. No magnitude system is asserted. A24 cached sources were read only; owner and publisher pages were fetched live on 2026-10-26. The inventory labels the 1740nm channel 1.735 μm; DARTS rounds it to 1.74 μm. Satoh et al. Figure 2 distinguishes standalone filters from products with the common short-wavelength-pass filter and discusses temperature shifts. No assertion is made that NJM curves have been corrected for these effects.
